waveName: Wave 5 – Undo/redo & stone editing, scale performance, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI

package.title: Full-width material and shopping view with exact per-material buying list
package.goal: The Material & Einkauf tab shows what to buy per material: packs, stock and shortfall, cost, and missing materials. It exports a shopping CSV and prints cleanly.
steps:
Stat row:
- Steine gesamt.
- Rohsteine inkl. Reserve, labelled as a safe upper bound.
- Kosten, with two decimals and the 'unvollständig' badge.
- Fugenmasse, labelled Schätzung.
- The reserve chips.

Table 'Einkaufsliste je Material' from stats.perMaterial: swatch, manufacturer, product, colour number, used for colours, raw size, need, stock, to buy, packs to buy (× package), price. Show '–' wherever piecesPerPack or price is missing; never estimate a pack count.

Table 'Bedarf je Farbe': Nr, swatch, name (paletteDisplayName), material or 'Material fehlt' or 'kein Material', stones, of which cut, Rohsteine, +Reserve. Show the per-shape and per-size tables side by side on desktop and as cards at ≤600 px.
Shortfall banner listing the materials whose need exceeds stock, with the total to buy.

shoppingCsv.ts: buildShoppingCsv(stats, palette, materials, lang), ';' plus decimal comma unless the language is English. Export button through downloadBlob with SaveResultNote. 'Drucken' calls window.print() with @media print rules that hide the navigation and viewer.
acceptance: Unit test: the CSV totals equal stats.rawWithReserveTotal and stats.totalCost. A material shared by two colours appears as one row with 1 pack in the 100/50 stock fixture.
e2e at 1440 and 390 px: no table needs horizontal scrolling at 1440, and the packs column is visible.
package.risk: Effort M. No currency symbol unless a currency setting exists.

findings.title: Material calculation (the shopping list) is squeezed into a 340 px sidebar tab with a clipped column
findings.problem: The most practical output for a hobbyist, how many stones and packs of each colour to buy, sits in a 340 px tab next to a large canvas. The table overflows, the 'Pack.' column is cut off, colour names and assigned materials are missing, and two thirds of the screen is empty while scrolling the 32 rows.

Screenshots shots/j2-12-plan-material.png, shots/j7-01-scrolled-material.png. Layout: src/ui/styles.css:670-673 (grid 1fr 340px), src/ui/project/StepPlan.tsx:239.
findings.proposal: Change StepPlan into two top-level views: 'Verlegen' (viewer plus sections) and 'Material & Einkauf' (full width, no viewer). Render MaterialCalc as a full-width table: Nr, swatch, name, assigned material (manufacturer, number), Steine, davon geschnitten, Rohsteine, +Reserve, Packungen, Preis, Bestand/Fehlmenge. Put the summary KPIs (Steine gesamt, Rohsteine inkl. Reserve, Kosten, Fugenmasse) in a stat row on top, and add 'Einkaufsliste als CSV' and 'drucken' buttons.
corrected:
1) In StepPlan.tsx, move the Abschnitte/Material switch out of the aside and above `.viewer-layout`, and rename the options to 'Verlegen' and 'Material & Einkauf'. When 'Material & Einkauf' is selected, render MaterialCalc at full width in place of the viewer-layout. Keep the Viewer mounted but hidden, or accept that it re-mounts.

2) In MaterialCalc:
- Show the KPIs as a `.summary-box` stat row: Steine gesamt, Rohsteine inkl. Reserve, Kosten (with the existing `costComplete` 'incomplete' badge), Fugenmasse (marked as an estimate). Keep the reserve chips next to them.
- Turn the per-colour table into a full-width table that mirrors the PDF material list (pdf.ts:371-386), using only existing ColorStat fields. Columns: Nr, swatch, name (palette[i].name), material (manufacturer, product, colorNumber, or 'kein Material zugeordnet' with a link to step 5), Steine, davon geschnitten, Rohstein-Format (rawW x rawH), Rohsteine, +Reserve, Packungen ('packs x piecesPerPack', or '–' when no material or no pack size; never estimate a pack count), Preis (cs.cost or '–'), and Bestand/Fehlmenge (shown only when material.stock is set).
- Write the header 'Packungen' in full instead of 'Pack.'.
- Lay the per-shape and per-size tables side by side underneath.

3) Add 'Einkaufsliste als CSV' as a new `buildShoppingCsv(stats, palette, materials, decimalComma)` in src/core/csv.ts with exactly those columns. Run it through the existing pdf worker path. Add a small unit test that its totals equal stats.rawWithReserveTotal and totalCost.

4) Add 'Drucken' as `window.print()` with an `@media print` rule that hides the nav, stepper and viewer.

Below 980 px, the existing single-column media query already applies, so mobile needs no change apart from keeping `.table-wrap` horizontal scrolling. Effort: S for the layout and table, M including the CSV and print rules.

A) Fix the core first (src/core/stats.ts, about M effort).
- Add `perMaterial: { materialId, material, colors: number[], rawW, rawH, need, stock?, toBuy?, packs?, packsToBuy?, cost? }[]`.
- `need` = sum of the per-colour `rawWithReserve` values of the colours linked to that material. This keeps Σ per material = Σ per colour = `rawWithReserveTotal` exactly.
- `packs = ceil(need / piecesPerPack)`, only when `piecesPerPack > 0`; otherwise leave it undefined and show '–'.
- `toBuy = max(0, need − stock)`, only when `stock !== undefined`. A stock of 0 counts as recorded; today StepPlan.tsx:419 ignores it because of `stock > 0`.
- `packsToBuy = ceil(toBuy / piecesPerPack)`.
- `cost = packs × price`.
- Compute `totalCost` from `perMaterial`, not per colour. `costComplete` stays false if any colour with stones has no material, no pieces per pack or no price.
- Colours without a material go into a group "ohne Material" with the raw size taken from the layout tile, packs '–' and cost marked as incomplete.
- Add a vitest. Two colours share one material with piecesPerPack 100 and stock 50; colour needs 30 + 30. Expect 1 pack (not 2) and toBuy 10 (not 0). Also assert Σ need over perMaterial == rawWithReserveTotal.
- Use `perMaterial` in the PDF material table as well (pdf.ts:371-384).

B) UI (StepPlan.tsx and styles.css, S effort).
- Move the Abschnitte / Material switch above `.viewer-layout`.
- 'Abschnitte': keeps the viewer and the 340 px side panel as today.
- 'Material & Einkauf': renders MaterialCalc at full width, without the viewer.
- Top: a stat row with Steine gesamt, Rohsteine inkl. Reserve, Kosten (with the existing 'unvollständig' badge, and two decimals) and Fugenmasse (keep "Schätzung"), plus the reserve chips.
- Table 1, "Einkaufsliste je Material": swatch, manufacturer, product, colour number, used for colours (e.g. 04, 05, 07), raw size w×h mm, Bedarf incl. reserve, Bestand, zu kaufen, Packungen zu kaufen (× packageSize), Preis.
- Table 2, "Bedarf je Farbe": Nr, swatch, name, material, stones, of which cut, Rohsteine, +Reserve. No packs or price in this table.
- Keep the per-shape and per-size tables below, side by side on desktop.
- Add an "Einkaufsliste als CSV" button: semicolon-separated, decimal comma unless the language is English, rows taken directly from `perMaterial`.
- Drop the 'drucken' button, or link it to the PDF materials page.
- On screens under 600 px, show each material row as a card, so there is no table that has to be scrolled sideways.

C) Do not add a currency symbol unless a currency setting exists (Material.price has none). Never show a pack count or cost for a material that has no piecesPerPack or price.

corrected:
Keep the table (it is the variant that measurably works) and change four things in StepColors.tsx (PaletteEditor) and styles.css.

1. **Reorder columns** so the ones the user acts on come right after the name: Nr.+swatch (one cell), Name, Steine, Bedarf, Material (select + ΔE), HEX·L*a*b*, delete. 3. **Phone only (`@media (max-width: 600px)`).**

4. **Plan step.** In MaterialCalc (StepPlan.tsx:391-427), merge the swatch into the Nr. cell and apply the same nowrap. That alone removes the 52 px overflow that hides 'Pack.'. A card layout is not needed there.

1) StepColors.tsx, at 600 px wide or less: show each palette colour as a compact card instead of a table row. Either render the existing `tr`/`td` as a CSS grid (`td[data-label]::before { content: attr(data-label) }`), so there is only one copy of the markup and the edit handlers, or use a small `useMediaQuery('(max-width:600px)')` that switches to a card component sharing the same handlers. - Line 2, bold: `{n(cs.pieces)} {t('colors.stones')} · {n(cs.rawWithReserve)} {t('colors.rawShort')} inkl. {reservePct} % Reserve`. Use only these existing stats values and show '–' when stats are missing; do not compute anything new.

findings.title: Material matching ignores stock, silently merges colours and never reports which image colours the owned tiles cannot match (req. 8)
findings.problem: Requirement 8 asks the app to prefer owned colours and to suggest the nearest one when a colour is missing. In 'auto → eigene Materialien' mode, several image colours that snap to the same material are merged without notice. The ΔE gap is computed and then thrown away (PaletteColor.deltaE is declared but never set). Material.stock is never used in the assignment, so over-use only shows up afterwards as a red minus number. There is no notion of owned versus to-buy, and no list of colours to buy.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/spec-gaps/core3.ts (output in core3.out), using 12 generic test-only materials with stock 200: '32 requested → auto-snap palette size 10'; mean ΔE 1.58 → 9.99 (p95 16); 'deltaE fields populated: 0'. Worst gap: image colour #2D503C, nearest material #2E7D32, ΔE 19.1. Every over-used colour exceeds its stock, e.g. '#6FA8DC needs 1610 raw, stock 200 → short by 1410 (assignment ignored stock)'. Code: FixedColor has no stock (src/core/mosaic.ts:16-21). useProject.ts:292 drops stock when building the palette. Stock is only shown afterwards (src/ui/project/StepPlan.tsx:419-421). types.ts:59 declares deltaE, and nothing assigns it.
findings.proposal: 1) In auto-snap, write the centre→material ΔE (already computed as bd in mosaic.ts around line 450) into PaletteColor.deltaE. Report merges, e.g. '32 angefragt → 10 Materialfarben (22 Bildfarben zusammengelegt)'. 2) Add a 'Fehlende Farben' panel listing image colours whose nearest owned material is > ΔE 5 away, with Lab, HEX and stone count. This is an honest shopping specification and invents no product. 3) Add Material.owned (or treat stock>0 as owned) and a 'bevorzugen' weight: cost = ΔE + λ·[nicht vorhanden]. 4) Add a stock-constrained post-pass in the worker. Keep the per-piece source Lab, which is already quantised as c1Lab/c2Lab/subLab in computeMosaic. For each colour whose need exceeds stock, reassign the pieces with the smallest ΔE increase to the next colours that still have stock (greedy by marginal cost, or min-cost flow), until need ≤ stock. Report the stones changed and the new mean or p95 ΔE. If no assignment is possible, say so instead of hiding it.
corrected:
1) Honest per-colour ΔE (S), in src/core/mosaic.ts.
- In `track()` (around line 481), keep per-palette-index arrays `sumDE[pi]`, `maxDE[pi]` and `cnt[pi]`.
- When building the palette (line 572), set `deltaE = sumDE/cnt` (rounded) and add an optional `maxDeltaE` field to `PaletteColor` in types.ts. This is the real stone-to-assigned-colour gap and works in every mode.
- In auto-snap, also store `mergedFrom` = the number of k-means centres that snapped to each material (from the existing `used` map).

2) Fix the misleading UI column (S), in src/ui/project/StepColors.tsx around lines 178-200.
- In auto-snap and materials mode, show `p.deltaE` (mean, with max as tooltip), warning above 5, instead of the trivial palette-to-material ΔE of 0,0.
- Above the palette table, add a notice such as "32 angefragt → 10 Materialfarben (22 Bildfarben zusammengelegt)" when `palette.length < colorCount`.
- Add the i18n keys to de, en and tr.

3) "Fehlende Farben" list (S-M).
- In auto-snap, also return the k-means centres from `computeMosaic`, each with its Lab, HEX, nearest material and ΔE, and its stone weight. For the weight, count the sampled weights `ws` per centre with a nearest-centre pass over `pts`.
- Show every centre whose nearest-material ΔE is above 5 as a shopping specification: HEX, Lab, approximate stone share, and "nächstes eigenes Material XY, ΔE n". Label it as a colour target, not a product. Add it to the PDF material list as well.
- In plain auto mode, reuse the existing link-materials ΔE instead.

4) Stock (default unchanged).
- Add a summary banner in StepPlan and StepColors listing every colour where raw tiles with reserve exceed `stock` (stock > 0 only, so empty stock still means unknown), with the total shortfall to buy.
- Optional, opt-in setting "Nur vorhandenen Bestand verwenden" (L), implemented inside `computeMosaic`, which holds the per-piece Lab:
  - after the normal assignment, compute raw-tile need per colour using the same yields as stats.ts (diagonal triangle = 2 pieces per tile, etc.) plus the reserve;
  - greedily move the pieces with the smallest ΔE increase to the next-nearest colour that still has stock until need ≤ stock;
  - report the number of stones changed and the new mean and p95 ΔE;
  - if total stock is below total need, refuse with an explicit message instead of producing a partial result.

Drop the separate `Material.owned` flag. The DB is already the user's own stock.

Order: honest reporting first (S/M), then preferring owned colours (S). Any automatic stock rebalancing stays opt-in.

A) Exact ΔE per colour from the real stones (mosaic.ts, assignment loop at lines ~479-548).
- Next to `track(l, pi)`, keep per palette index: piece count, sum of ΔE, max ΔE, and the number of pieces above ΔE 5 and above ΔE 10. Use the source Lab, which the loop already has (c1Lab, c2Lab, subLab), not the dithered target.
- Remap these through `keep`/`remap` and store them on PaletteColor as `matchDeltaE?: { mean, max, over5, over10 }`. Either repurpose the existing `deltaE?` field or replace it.
- In StepColors, for 'auto-snap' and 'materials' mode, show "Ø ΔE x / max y (n Steine > 5)" instead of the palette-vs-own-material ΔE, which is always 0.
- Clear `matchDeltaE` in `updatePaletteColor` when the hex or material changes, in single-stone recolours, and in `removePaletteColor` (src/core/edits.ts). Then show "– (nach manueller Änderung neu berechnen)" rather than a stale number.
- In StepCompute, add "32 angefragt → 10 Materialfarben (22 Bildfarben zusammengelegt)". These numbers come from km.centers.length and used.size.

B) Panel "Fehlende Farben / Einkaufsempfehlung" (auto-snap mode).
- Run the k-means as today, plus a second NearestColorMatcher over km.centers. In the assignment loop, find each piece's nearest centre from its source Lab and count pieces per centre exactly. Do not use the sampled k-means weights, which are estimates.
- For each centre whose nearest material is more than ΔE 5 away (adjustable), list: HEX, Lab, exact stone count, the material used instead, and the ΔE.
- Label it "Farbton zum Nachkaufen (Zielwert)". Never name a product.
- For 'materials' mode: run k-means only on pieces whose ΔE is above the threshold, list the resulting centres the same way, or mark this as "nicht verfügbar" in the README limitations table.

C) Owned versus to-buy.
- Add an explicit `Material.owned?: boolean`, default true, to keep existing data. Add a checkbox in Materials.tsx and a CSV column.
- In auto-snap, pick the material by cost = ΔE + λ·[not owned], with a "bevorzugen" slider (0 = only colour accuracy). Report how many centres switched to an owned colour and the ΔE change.

D) Instead of the automatic stock post-pass, an exact shortfall and shopping list (StepPlan, computed with stats.ts).
- Per material: need incl. reserve, stock, shortfall in pieces, packs to buy (ceil(shortfall/piecesPerPack)), and cost from price.
- Treat stock 0 as "nicht vorrätig". Fix the `stock > 0` condition at StepPlan.tsx:419, which currently hides a stock-0 shortfall.
- Add a CSV/PDF export of this list.
- Optional manual action "Bestand reicht nicht → Steine dieser Farbe teilweise ersetzen". Preview the count and the ΔE increase from per-piece source Lab, exclude face/eye regions by default, re-run stats afterwards, and refuse with a clear message when total stock is below total need.
- Any automatic stock-constrained reassignment must use the stats.ts raw-yield function, not piece counts, so stock and need stay in the same unit.

Tests:
- `matchDeltaE` counts add up to the total piece count.
- Missing-colour stone counts add up to the total piece count.
- After edits, `matchDeltaE` is cleared.
- The shortfall equals rawWithReserve − stock, including stock = 0.

findings.title: Material links are lost on project export/import, and deleting a used material silently changes the material calculation
findings.problem: exportProject writes only record, image, mosaic and progress. The materials referenced by palette[i].materialId and settings.materialIds are not included. After importing on a second device (the README recommends this for PC↔tablet), every material link is dangling. The stone detail shows 'Material: ?', raw-stone counts fall back to the grid size, and pack and cost information disappears. None of this is flagged. The same happens on the same device when a used material is deleted: Materials.tsx only asks 'Material löschen?'. Material DB edits (hex, size) and new materials (materialIds=[] means 'all') also never mark a materials-mode project as stale. A second minor point: an import gets exactly the same name as the existing project.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t9_materials_export_import.cjs plus mats.csv, output t9_output.txt. Device 1: 'Material: Bisazza Vetricolor 09', 'Rohsteine inkl. Reserve 1.982', 'Kosten 0,55'. 'export contains materials? false | palette entries with materialId: 10 / 10'. After deleting 6 materials on device 1: 'stale badge = false', 'Rohsteine inkl. Reserve 3.387', 'Kosten 0,25 unvollständig'. Device 2 after import: 'Material: ?', 'Rohsteine inkl. Reserve 6.367', no cost row (screenshot t9-device2-matcalc.png). Code: projects.ts:208-226 (payload without materials), Materials.tsx:188-191 (delete with no usage check), useProject.ts:27 (key uses only materialIds).
findings.proposal: (1) Export: add `materials: Material[]` holding every material referenced by the palette or settings.materialIds. Import: upsert them by id, or match an existing material by manufacturer+colorNumber+hex. Report 'X Materialien übernommen, Y zugeordnet'. Append ' (Import)' to the imported project's name. (2) On delete in Materials, scan listProjects() for references and show 'Wird in Projekt A, B verwendet – Materialbedarf ändert sich'. (3) In PaletteEditor and StoneDialog, show a warning badge 'Material fehlt' when materialId is set but not found, instead of '?'. In MaterialCalc, list colours whose raw size fell back to the grid size. (4) For materials and auto-snap modes, add a fingerprint of the used materials (id+hex+size) to computeKey.
corrected:
(1) Export: in src/storage/projects.ts exportProject, add `materials: Material[]` to the payload. Include every material whose id appears in record.palette[].materialId or settings.materialIds; when materialIds is [] ('all'), include only the palette-referenced ones. Import, in importProject:
- For each exported material: if a local material with the same id exists, keep the local one and do not overwrite it.
- Otherwise, if a local material matches by manufacturer+product+colorNumber (trimmed, case-insensitive), map the old id to the local id.
- Otherwise, insert the exported material with its original id.
- Rewrite palette[].materialId and settings.materialIds through that mapping before saveProject.
- Return the counts and show 'X Materialien übernommen, Y zugeordnet' in Projects.tsx.
- Append ' (Import)' to meta.name when a project with the same name already exists.

(2) Material CSV (Materials.tsx materialsToCsv/parseMaterialsCsv): add an 'id' column. On CSV import, reuse the id if present and upsert by id; otherwise fall back to a manufacturer+product+colorNumber match before creating a new uid(). This lets the CSV route keep links intact.

(3) Delete: in the Materials.tsx delete handler, load the projects and count the ones whose palette or settings.materialIds reference m.id. If any do, the confirm text names them ('Wird in Projekt A, B verwendet – Materialbedarf/Kosten ändern sich').

(4) Missing-material visibility instead of silent fallback:
- In makeRawSizeFn, return a `missing: true` flag when materialId is set but not found. Collect these colours into a `missingMaterials: number[]` field on Stats and set costComplete=false for them.
- StoneDialog.tsx:129-131: show a warning badge 'Material fehlt (gelöscht oder nicht importiert)' instead of '?'.
- StepColors.tsx, material column: show the same badge.
- StepPlan.tsx material calc: list the affected colour codes with 'Rohsteinmaß = Rastermaß (Material fehlt)'. Render the cost row whenever any colour has a material reference, even if totalCost is 0, with the 'unvollständig' badge.
- PDF material list: same marking.

Do NOT add a material fingerprint to computeKey or otherwise mark the project stale. A recompute wipes manual edits and laying progress, and with materialIds=[] any new material would invalidate every materials-mode project. If desired, show a non-blocking info note ('Materialdaten seit der Berechnung geändert') that does not suggest recomputing.

(1) **Export/import (src/storage/projects.ts:75-118).**
- Raise the payload version to 2 and add `materials: Material[]`. Include only materials referenced by `palette[i].materialId`, plus the explicit `settings.materialIds` when that list is not empty. Do not export the whole catalog when the list is [] ('all').
- On import, handle each exported material in this order:
  - (a) If a local material with the same id exists, keep the local one. Never overwrite it. If its hex or size differs from the exported one, record that as a note.
  - (b) Otherwise, look for an exact match on normalised manufacturer + product + colorNumber + lengthMm × widthMm. If found, remap that id in the palette and in `settings.materialIds`.
  - (c) Otherwise, insert the exported material under its own id.
- Never pick a 'nearest' material automatically.
- Show a summary message: 'X Materialien neu angelegt, Y vorhandenen zugeordnet, Z mit abweichenden Daten'.
- For a version 1 file, warn: 'Datei enthält keine Materialien – N Farben ohne gültiges Material'.
- Append ' (Import)' to the imported project's name.
- Add an optional `id` column to the materials CSV (Materials.tsx:25) and reuse it on CSV import, so a CSV round trip keeps the links.

(2) **Delete in Materials.tsx:186-193.** Before calling confirm, run listProjects() (db.ts:91). Count the projects whose palette or settings.materialIds reference the material, and say so in the confirm text: 'Wird in Projekt A, B (n Farben) verwendet – Materialbedarf und Kosten dieser Farben werden danach ohne Material berechnet.' Optionally offer to replace it with another material before deleting.

(3) **Make the fallback visible.**

(4) **Replace the computeKey fingerprint with a non-destructive check.** Do not change computeKey or computedWith. globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
